title: High prevalence of antagonizing rhetoric in trending topics on Twitter/X
abstract: arXiv:2610.22455v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Disagreement between political opponents is a central element of democracy. This disagreement can be voiced in different ways. An opponent can be antagonized, i.e. portrayed as an enemy that needs to be overcome, or they can be criticized, i.e. treated as a legitimate adversary with whom one can engage. While the latter is a fundamental part of democratic exchange, the former can be detrimental to public discourse. Political disagreement increasingly takes place on social media, where negativity towards political out-groups has been found to drive engagement. However, existing research has largely treated such negativity as a single dimension, leaving open whether it is antagonization or criticism that circulates on these platforms. This work addresses this gap by introducing a computational approach to detect these two types of rhetoric in text and identify its targets. translated_title: Twitter/X 热门话题中对抗性言论的高流行度
translated_abstract: 政治对手之间的分歧是民主的核心要素，而这种分歧可以以不同方式表达：可以将对手敌对化，即将其描绘为需要被战胜的敌人；也可以对其进行批评，即将其视为可以理性交锋的合法对手。后者是民主交流的基本组成部分，而前者则可能损害公共话语。政治分歧日益发生在社交媒体上，已有研究发现对政治外群体的负面态度会驱动用户参与度。然而，现有研究大多将这种负面性视为单一维度，未能回答在这些平台上流传的究竟是敌对化言论还是批评性言论。本工作通过引入一种计算方法来检测文本中的这两种言论类型并识别其攻击目标，填补了这一空白。在一个包含超过1700万条来自热门话题的推文的语料库中……
tldr: 本研究提出了一种能够区分并检测文本中“敌对化”与“批评”两种政治言论及其目标的计算方法，并揭示了Twitter/X热门话题中敌对化言论的高度盛行。
en_tdlr: This study introduces a computational approach to detect and distinguish antagonizing from criticizing rhetoric and identify its targets, revealing a high prevalence of antagonizing rhetoric in trending topics on Twitter/X.
